text: I’ll model the sealed oil domain as the 60 mm axial extrusion of the bore cross-section minus the keyed 40 mm shaft. The shaft steps identify the pressure sides but lie outside the sealed domain, so the two axial cross-sections are the high- and low-pressure patches. I’ll use an exact CAD fluid volume for inspection, then make an extrusion mesh tailored to the 0.05 mm gap so it is resolved without globally refining the much larger keyway.

The coarse inspection confirms a single connected leakage domain and visibly resolves the narrow annulus and the much deeper keyway. Next I’ll identify the CAD faces by their actual surface type, area, normal, and centre—not by bounding-box position—so the six requested patch groups can be exported correctly.

The face audit exposed a CAD alignment issue: the initial inspection sketch was correct, but build123d’s primitive defaults centred the box and cylinder, offsetting the actual keyway. I’ll correct the primitive alignments explicitly and repeat the measurements before any export.

I’ll rebuild with x/y centred and z starting at 0 for both cylinders, while the key cutter uses minimum alignment from \((-6,15,0)\) mm. This keeps the requested 5 mm crown-to-floor depth and symmetric 12 mm width.

The corrected CAD now has exactly seven faces: bore, shaft, floor, two flanks, and two ends. I’ll export six patch files (the two flanks grouped together) with a 5 µm linear tessellation tolerance, then inspect the combined surface for closure and patch triangle counts before creating the volume mesh.

Patch selection will use surface class and intrinsic face normals: cylindrical bore, trimmed cylindrical shaft, axial-normal end planes, downward-normal keyway floor, and x-normal flanks. This avoids any bounding-box endpoint heuristic.

Before the 3D extrusion, I’ll mesh only the exact 2D cross-section at a deliberately coarse 0.5 mm tangential/keyway scale. The 50 µm gap constrains the radial spacing automatically; this preview will show whether the mesher preserves a connected annulus-plus-keyway domain.

The 2D mesh itself generated, but PyVista could not read Gmsh’s native file format because its optional meshio reader is unavailable. I’ll repeat the same one-step preview and have Gmsh write VTK directly for inspection.

The preview is geometrically correct, but the replay checker rightly notes that the imports only occurred in the failed visualization cell. I’ll re-emit the successful preview with its own imports so `build.py` is reproducible from an empty directory.

The coarse section has 777 points and 1,560 entities and remains connected around the full circumference. I’ll now extrude that section through 60 mm using 60 axial layers (1 mm each). Patch identification in the Gmsh model will use surface type and measured CAD area; the end planes are identified by their extrusion origin/destination, not by a generic bounding-box face query.

Gmsh labels extruded curved faces as “Surface of Extrusion” rather than “Cylinder,” so the type-based filter was too strict. I’ll inspect the side-surface areas and extrusion provenance, then encode the patch mapping from those measured entities.

The measured extrusion entities are unambiguous: one 0.00755867 m² outer surface is the bore; the two remaining swept curved surfaces sum to the 0.00680856 m² shaft area; the 0.000720 m² plane is the floor; and the two 0.000244727 m² planes are the flanks. I’ll use those intrinsic areas to build the final physical groups.
The volume mesh is now on disk: 61,920 extruded prism cells. I’ll convert it immediately to OpenFOAM, inspect the generated patch table, and run `checkMesh` before any further refinement.
`gmshToFoam` requires a minimal OpenFOAM `controlDict` even for conversion; the geometry and Gmsh mesh are unaffected. I’ll add only that required case metadata, then convert and check.
Conversion produced exactly the six requested OpenFOAM patches and 61,920 prism cells. I’ll now run the binding topology/geometry checks and report the worst quality metrics.

This OpenFOAM build also loads `fvSchemes`/`fvSolution` when `checkMesh -allGeometry` is requested, even though no solver is run. I’ll add empty dictionaries solely to satisfy that reader and rerun the same check.

The geometry check expects the standard scheme subdictionaries, not merely an empty file. I’ll provide conventional defaults; they are case metadata only and do not constitute a solve or boundary-condition setup.

The first 3D check is topologically sound but fails one quality criterion: 912 prisms have determinant below 0.001. The 1 mm axial spacing is too long relative to the 50 µm clearance. I’ll reduce the axial layer thickness to 0.25 mm (240 layers), preserving the same cross-section and patch mapping.
The refined mesh contains 247,680 prisms. I’ll reconvert it over the coarse OpenFOAM mesh and rerun the full topology/geometry check.

The refined mesh passes all checks: one region, six patches, determinant minimum 0.00297, aspect ratio 10.17, and `Mesh OK`. I’ll make one final cutaway inspection of the actual 3D mesh on disk to verify axial extrusion, end faces, annulus, and keyway continuity visually.

Completed geometry and OpenFOAM mesh in the requested case.

- Fluid domain: 60 mm sealed length, 40.1 mm bore, 40.0 mm shaft, measured radial clearance 0.050 mm.
- Keyway: 12 mm wide and 5 mm crown-to-floor depth, continuous through the sealed length.
- Mesh: 247,680 prism cells, 240 axial layers at 0.25 mm; one connected region.
- Patches: `shaft`, `keywayFloor`, `keywayFlanks`, `bore`, `highPressure`, `lowPressure`.
- Exported one STL per patch under `constant/triSurface`.
- Full `checkMesh -allGeometry -allTopology`: **Mesh OK**. Maximum aspect ratio 10.17, maximum skewness 1.31, minimum determinant 0.00297.

Assumptions: the keyway is a straight rectangular axial groove with depth measured radially from the shaft crown; the 50 mm and 30 mm shaft steps lie immediately outside the modeled 60 mm sealed span and identify the high- and low-pressure sides, respectively. The requested radial clearance is represented, but this coarse production mesh has one cell through the 0.05 mm annular gap; no flow solution or boundary conditions were created.
